Can supplement other scholarships up to a maximum of €1,000/month total
Separate from GRADUATE+ Scholarship (also €1,000/month for 10 months, SFRI-funded)

raw_items: Must be a foreign national
Must be applying to a Master's programme at ENS de Lyon (M1 or M2)
For M1 candidates: must have obtained a Licence (equivalent to 180 ECTS / Bachelor's degree)
Outstanding academic record required
Open to all disciplines: STEM, Arts, Humanities, Social Sciences
Renewable for 2nd year subject to selection by head of Master's programme and passing M1

benefits: €1,000 per month for one academic year (10 months)
Renewable for a second year under conditions
Can supplement other scholarships up to €1,000/month maximum combined
scholarships.target_group: Outstanding international (non-French) students seeking Master's degrees at ENS de Lyon in any discipline, from sciences and engineering to arts, humanities, and social sciences.
scholarships.description: The ENS de Lyon Ampère Excellence Scholarships provide €1,000/month for one academic year to outstanding international students enrolled in any of ENS de Lyon's Master's programmes. ENS de Lyon is one of France's most prestigious grandes écoles, known for excellence in research across sciences, humanities, and the arts.
application_process: Apply to a Master's programme at ENS de Lyon via the admissions portal
Simultaneously apply for the Ampère Scholarship following the process outlined at ens-lyon.fr/en/studies/admissions/application-masters-degrees-and-scholarships
Submit required academic documents and scholarship application by the deadline
Scholarship renewal in 2nd year requires selection by Master's programme head and passing M1
Contact: international@ens-lyon.fr

scholarships.name: Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Doctoral (CGRS-D)
scholarships.provider: Government of Canada / CIHR / NSERC / SSHRC
scholarships.deadline: October 17 (direct to agency); institutions set earlier internal deadlines
application_period: Year-round - agency deadline October 17; institution deadlines vary
important_dates: Can be held at Canadian or international institutions (20% of awards available abroad)
Up to 15% of awards available to international applicants
Vanier CGS discontinued March 2025 - replaced by CGRS-D

raw_items: Must be enrolled in or applying to a doctoral program (predominantly research-oriented)
Must have completed no more than 36 months of full-time equivalent doctoral study by December 31 of application year
International applicants: must be enrolled at an eligible Canadian institution by the application deadline
Up to 15% of awards available to international applicants
International applicants can only apply through a Canadian institution (not directly to agency)
Cannot have previously received a doctoral-level scholarship from CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC (including old Vanier)
Can apply maximum 3 times
Selection criteria: Research Potential (50%) + Relevant Experience and Achievements (50%)
Apply to the agency matching your research field: CIHR (health), NSERC (science/engineering), SSHRC (social sciences/humanities)

benefits: Can be held at Canadian institutions or international institutions (Canadian citizens/PRs only for international hold)
Supplement funding may be available for priority research areas
Travel supplements may be available via CRTAS-RTS
scholarships.target_group: Outstanding Canadian and international doctoral students in health sciences, natural sciences, engineering, social sciences, and humanities, seeking funding for their PhD research at Canadian universities.
scholarships.description: The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship - Doctoral (CGRS-D) is Canada's premier doctoral scholarship, providing $40,000/year for 3 years to outstanding PhD researchers. It replaced the Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarships in March 2025 as part of the harmonized Canada Research Training Awards Suite (CRTAS). International students enrolled at Canadian institutions may apply.
application_process: Determine your research field agency: CIHR (health), NSERC (science/engineering), SSHRC (social sciences/humanities)
International applicants must apply through their Canadian institution (NOT directly to agency)
Contact your faculty of graduate studies for institutional deadline (well before October 17)
Submit application through the relevant agency online portal (CIHR: ResearchNET, NSERC/SSHRC: online systems)
Applications reviewed by institution, then forwarded to agency review committee
Results announced: April 30
Contacts: CIHR: support-soutien@cihr-irsc.gc.ca | NSERC: nsercscholarships-boursesCRSNG@NSERC-CRSNG.GC.CA | SSHRC: fellowships@sshrc-crsh.gc.ca

scholarships.name: Canada Impact+ Research Training Awards - Doctoral
scholarships.provider: Government of Canada / CIHR / NSERC / SSHRC
scholarships.program_type: Tri-agency doctoral scholarship - impact-focused (part of CRTAS)
fields: All research disciplines aligned with Canada's priority areas
scholarships.deadline: Check agency websites for current deadlines
application_period: Check CIHR, NSERC, SSHRC websites for current intake
important_dates: Launched as part of the 2024 Budget harmonization of CRTAS programs

raw_items: Must be enrolled in a doctoral program at an eligible Canadian institution
Demonstrate research excellence and potential for impact
Aligned with Canada's priority research areas
International applicants: check current agency guidelines for eligibility

benefits: Support for high-impact doctoral research aligned with national priorities
scholarships.target_group: Outstanding doctoral researchers pursuing high-impact work aligned with Canada's strategic research priorities, as part of the 2025 CRTAS harmonization.
scholarships.description: The Canada Impact+ Research Training Awards - Doctoral provides $40,000/year for 3 years to outstanding PhD students pursuing research with significant societal impact, as part of Canada's 2025 CRTAS program suite that replaced the Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarships.
application_process: Check current program details at nserc-crsng.canada.ca
Apply through the relevant tri-agency portal (CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC)
Contact your institution's graduate studies office for guidance

scholarships.name: Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarships - University of Toronto
fields: All disciplines offered at University of Toronto
scholarships.deadline: November 7 (student application); school nomination deadline October 10
application_period: July 1 – November 7 (school nomination July–October; student application October–November)
important_dates: U of T admissions application deadline: October 17 (via OUAC)
Student Pearson scholarship application deadline: November 7
Scholarship recipients notified: starting end of January
Studies begin: September of award year
Each year approximately 37 Pearson Scholars are selected

raw_items: Must be an international student (non-Canadian, requiring a study permit)
Must be in final year of senior secondary school in the application year, OR have graduated no earlier than June of the previous year
Must begin studies at University of Toronto in September of the award year
Students already attending post-secondary studies are NOT eligible
Must be nominated by your current secondary school (one nomination per school per year)
Schools must be verified by U of T; new schools can apply to join the program
Must apply to at least one undergraduate program at U of T by October 17
Use of generative AI (e.g. ChatGPT) in scholarship application is prohibited and results in disqualification

benefits: Full tuition fees for four years
Full residence support for four years
Access to Pearson Program Office enrichment and support programs
amounts: Full tuition + books + incidental fees + full residence (4 years)
scholarships.target_group: Outstanding international secondary school students worldwide who demonstrate exceptional academic achievement, creativity, and leadership potential, nominated by their school to study at the University of Toronto.
scholarships.description: The Lester B. Pearson International Student Scholarships are the University of Toronto's most prestigious award for international students, covering full tuition, books, incidental fees and residence for four years. Approximately 37 scholars are selected annually from nominations submitted by secondary schools worldwide.
application_process: Ask your guidance counsellor or principal if your school is eligible to nominate a student
If school is not yet verified, they can apply to join the program at apply.adm.utoronto.ca/register/pearson-participate
School nominates one student via the secure nomination form (deadline: October 10)
Apply to at least one undergraduate program at U of T via OUAC by October 17
After nomination, receive a private link to the Pearson Scholarship application form
Submit scholarship application and all required documentation by November 7
Await results: recipients notified starting end of January; all nominees notified by April
Contact: apply.adm.utoronto.ca/register/pearson-inquiry

scholarships.name: A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (AGS) — International
scholarships.deadline: 1 February (Intake 1) and 1 August (Intake 2)
important_dates: Intake 1 interviews: mid-February to March | results: from mid-April
Intake 2 interviews: mid-August to October | results: from mid-November

raw_items: Open to all nationalities
Must have or be on track to obtain at least a Second-Class (Upper) Honours degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline
Non-Singaporean non-PR applicants must have the degree from a Singapore autonomous university
Must be in last semester of final year of undergraduate, OR already enrolled in a Singapore autonomous university PhD program (Mid-Term AGS)
Must gain PhD admission at NUS, NTU, SUTD, SMU, or SIT
Non-Singaporean / non-PR scholars: 3-year service commitment in Singapore-based companies after graduation

benefits: Full PhD tuition fees (up to 4 years)
Competitive monthly sustenance allowance (inclusive of CPF contribution where applicable)
Up to 12 months overseas research attachment funding
scholarships.target_group: Outstanding graduates worldwide seeking a fully funded PhD in science and engineering at Singapore autonomous universities, conducting research at A*STAR Research Institutes.
scholarships.description: The A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (AGS) funds up to 4 years of PhD or EngD studies at a Singapore autonomous university across four strategic tracks: STEM, Semiconductor, Quantum, and Computing. International scholars without Singapore PR must serve a 3-year commitment in Singapore-based companies after graduation.
application_process: Apply via A*STAR careers portal: careers.a-star.edu.sg
Select your preferred research track (STEM / Semiconductor / Quantum / Computing)
Submit academic transcripts, references, and proposed research area
Shortlisted candidates attend 2+ rounds of interviews with A*STAR Research Institute top management
Apply concurrently to the intended Singapore autonomous university for PhD admission
Scholarship award is conditional on securing PhD placement

scholarships.name: A*STAR International Fellowship (AIF) — Research Track
scholarships.deadline: 1 April (Cycle 1) and 1 October (Cycle 2)
important_dates: Cycle 1 opens: 1 January | closes: 1 April | interviews: mid-April to May | results: from mid-June
Cycle 2 opens: 1 July | closes: 1 October | interviews: mid-October to mid-November | results: from December
3-year service commitment at A*STAR after fellowship ends

raw_items: Must be a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident (SPR); non-SPR foreigners may be considered exceptionally but must obtain Singapore citizenship before commencement
Must have completed a PhD within the last 4 years (applicants finishing PhD may apply; award confirmed upon conferment)
Must not hold existing bonds to any institution
Must contact an approved overseas university/lab and establish a research project proposal before applying
Must have excellent publication record (Research track)
Must be applying for or have a confirmed postdoctoral position at a top overseas university/lab

benefits: Monthly overseas living allowance (rate varies by country and institution)
Monthly sustenance allowance inclusive of CPF contribution
scholarships.target_group: Early-career Singaporean/PR researchers who have recently completed their PhD and wish to deepen expertise through 1–2 years of overseas postdoctoral training at a world-class institution, before returning to contribute to A*STAR.
scholarships.description: The A*STAR International Fellowship (AIF) Research Track supports early-career Singaporean/PR researchers to undertake up to 2 years of postdoctoral training at leading overseas universities or research institutions. Fellows return to serve 3 years at an A*STAR Research Institute, contributing to Singapore's R&D ecosystem.
application_process: Identify an approved overseas university/lab and establish a research project with a prospective supervisor
Apply online at a-star.edu.sg/scholarships during an open cycle window
Seek endorsement from your intended A*STAR Research Institute supervisor and Executive Director before first interview
Attend 2 rounds of interviews (first round: 15-min presentation + 15-min Q&A)
Candidates overseas may attend virtually
AIF award is conditional on confirmed placement at approved overseas institution

scholarships.name: A*STAR International Fellowship (AIF) — Innovation Track
scholarships.program_type: Postdoctoral overseas fellowship — deep-tech / startup focus
scholarships.deadline: 1 April (Cycle 1) and 1 October (Cycle 2)
important_dates: Same timeline as AIF Research Track
Placement in deep-tech startups that are portfolio companies of top-tier VC/builder firms
3-year service commitment at A*STAR after fellowship ends

raw_items: Same general eligibility as AIF Research Track (Singapore Citizen/PR; PhD within last 4 years; no existing bonds)
Strong aptitude and aspiration to pursue roles in innovation and entrepreneurship (I&E)
Preferably good publication records
Placement in deep-tech startups (portfolio companies of top-tier VC/builder firms) or in VC/VB firms with entrepreneur-in-residence programmes

benefits: Same financial package as AIF Research Track
Monthly overseas living allowance + sustenance allowance
Annual return airfare + settling-in + computer + conference allowances
scholarships.target_group: Entrepreneurially-minded early-career Singaporean/PR researchers seeking to translate cutting-edge research into ventures through placements in top-tier deep-tech startups or VC firms overseas.
scholarships.description: The AIF Innovation Track is a postdoctoral fellowship for entrepreneurially-minded Singaporean/PR researchers to gain hands-on experience in deep-tech startups or VC firms overseas, enhancing their capabilities to commercialise research and build impactful ventures before returning to A*STAR.
application_process: Same application process as AIF Research Track
Identify a deep-tech startup (portfolio of top-tier VC/builder firm) or a VC firm as placement host
A*STAR maintains a list of approved partners — consult before applying
Apply at a-star.edu.sg/scholarships during an open cycle window

scholarships.name: JASSO Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students
scholarships.program_type: In-country scholarship for enrolled international students
scholarships.deadline: Apply through your Japanese university after enrollment — rolling/annual via school
application_period: Apply after enrolling at a Japanese university; school nominates to JASSO
important_dates: Reservation Program (EJU route): select option when applying for EJU exam before coming to Japan
Standard route: apply through school after enrollment in Japan (typically April intake)
Payment period: April–March (1 year) or October–March (6 months)

raw_items: Must be enrolled as a regular student at a Japanese university, graduate school, junior college, college of technology, specialized training college, or Japanese language institution
Must be a privately-financed international student (not receiving Japanese government / MEXT scholarship)
Resident status must be "Student"
Minimum GPA of 2.30 (on JASSO scale) from previous academic year
Japanese language proficiency: JLPT N2 or above, OR EJU Japanese 200+ pts, OR JASSO-recognized equivalent
OR English proficiency: CEFR B2 or above
Average monthly remittances below ¥90,000 (excluding tuition/entrance fees)
Not receiving another JASSO scholarship concurrently
Willing to cooperate with ETIC career survey after scholarship

benefits: ¥48,000/month (university, graduate school, junior college, college of technology, specialized training college)
scholarships.target_group: Privately-financed international students already enrolled at Japanese universities or graduate schools who have strong academic performance and financial need.
scholarships.description: The JASSO Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship provides a monthly stipend to privately-financed international students already studying in Japan who demonstrate academic excellence and financial need. Unlike MEXT, this is applied for after arriving in Japan through the student's school.
application_process: Pre-arrival route (Reservation Program): when registering for the EJU exam, opt into the Reservation Program — outstanding EJU scorers are pre-selected as reservation holders
In-Japan route: confirm with the international student office at your Japanese university about the application process (deadlines and nomination quotas vary by school)
Submit application documents through your school — individual direct applications to JASSO are not accepted
Required documents typically include: application form, transcript, financial statement, enrollment certificate

scholarships.name: JASSO Student Exchange Support Program (Scholarship for Study in Japan under Agreement)
scholarships.deadline: Apply through your home university — deadlines set by the exchange agreement
application_period: Contact your home university international office for current cycle
important_dates: Must return to home institution after program to continue degree
Available to countries with diplomatic relations with Japan (including Taiwan and Palestine)

raw_items: Must be enrolled at a higher education institution with a student exchange agreement with a Japanese university
Participating in an inbound short-term exchange program (8 days to 1 year)
Cannot participate solely for language courses — must be a degree program exchange
Good academic performance and character at home institution
Unable to finance the exchange solely at own expense (financial need)
Will return to home institution to continue studies and obtain degree after exchange
Total monthly allowance from all scholarships must not exceed ¥80,000
Must be able to obtain a Student status of residence (or any status for exchanges ≤90 days)

benefits: ¥80,000/month for the duration of the exchange (8 days to 1 year)
scholarships.target_group: International university students whose home institution has a student exchange agreement with a Japanese host university, participating in short-term academic exchange programs in Japan.
scholarships.description: The JASSO Student Exchange Support Program funds international exchange students who come to Japan under bilateral university agreements, providing ¥80,000/month for up to 1 year to support short-term academic exchanges.
application_process: Check if your Indonesian university has a student exchange agreement with a Japanese university
Apply through your home university's international exchange office
Your home university nominates eligible students to the Japanese host university
The Japanese host university coordinates with JASSO for scholarship disbursement

scholarships.name: KOICA Scholarship Program — Master's Degree
scholarships.program_type: Development-focused postgraduate scholarship for public sector professionals
scholarships.deadline: Approximately July annually (confirm via local KOICA office or Korean Embassy)
application_period: Check KOICA overseas office or Korean Embassy in your country for current cycle
important_dates: 2027 intake application period expected to close: around July 2026
Selection: two-stage — KOICA overseas selection + university academic evaluation
Studies begin: around March following selection
11 master's programmes in 2027 intake across leading Korean universities

raw_items: Must be from a KOICA partner/developing country (check KOICA eligibility list)
Must be a government official, public sector professional, or public development organization employee
Must have an official nomination or recommendation through government channels
Must hold a recognized bachelor's degree
Must satisfy admission requirements of the host Korean university
Priority given to those who can apply newly acquired knowledge to national development after graduation
Not intended for recent graduates — professional experience in a relevant sector required

benefits: Access to extracurricular and cultural activities
scholarships.target_group: Government officials and public sector professionals from KOICA partner (developing) countries seeking a master's degree at a leading Korean university in development-relevant fields.
scholarships.description: The KOICA Scholarship Program offers fully funded master's degrees at leading Korean universities (Yonsei, KDI School, Sungkyunkwan, University of Seoul, etc.) to public sector professionals from developing countries, with 11 specialised programs in the 2027 intake covering AI, digital health, public policy, agriculture, fisheries, and more.
application_process: Contact your local KOICA overseas office or the Korean Embassy in your country for the current cycle announcement
Obtain official nomination/recommendation through appropriate government channels
Submit application documents: transcripts, degree certificate, nomination letter, professional records, recommendation letters
Stage 1: KOICA selection administered through KOICA overseas office or Korean Embassy
Stage 2: Forwarded to chosen Korean university for academic evaluation
Confirm exact deadline for your country through the local KOICA office or Korean Embassy

scholarships.name: KOICA Scholarship Program — Doctoral Degree
scholarships.program_type: Development-focused doctoral scholarship for public sector professionals
scholarships.deadline: Approximately July annually (confirm via local KOICA office or Korean Embassy)
application_period: Check KOICA overseas office or Korean Embassy in your country for current cycle
important_dates: Participating universities: Kyungpook National University, Pukyong National University, University of Seoul, Yonsei University
Selection process: same two-stage process as master's

raw_items: Same general eligibility as KOICA Master's (KOICA partner country, public sector, government nomination)
Must hold a recognized master's degree
Advanced professional background in the relevant field strongly preferred
Must satisfy doctoral admission requirements of the host Korean university

scholarships.target_group: Public sector professionals from KOICA partner countries with a master's degree seeking doctoral-level expertise in agriculture, fisheries, AI/digital innovation, or infectious disease control at Korean universities.
scholarships.description: KOICA's doctoral scholarship track offers 4 fully funded PhD programmes at Korean universities in strategic development sectors, targeting senior public officials and researchers from partner countries who aim to build advanced research capacity.
application_process: Same process as KOICA Master's Scholarship — contact local KOICA office or Korean Embassy
Provide master's degree certificate in addition to standard documents
Two-stage selection: KOICA overseas office → host university academic evaluation

scholarships.name: Canada Postdoctoral Research Award (CPRA)
scholarships.provider: Government of Canada / CIHR / NSERC / SSHRC
scholarships.deadline: CIHR: September 17 | NSERC: October 17 | SSHRC: September 11 (annual)
application_period: Applications open approximately 4–5 months before deadline — check agency websites

raw_items: Must hold or expect to hold a doctorate or health professional degree before award start date
Must NOT hold or be on leave from a tenure-track or tenured faculty position
PhD/degree completion no more than 3 years before September 1 of application year (extensions possible for parental leave, illness, military service, etc.)
International applicants: must be currently enrolled in or have completed doctorate at a Canadian institution, OR conducting postdoc at a Canadian institution — as of application deadline
Up to 20% of awards available to international applicants
Can be held at Canadian institutions OR abroad (up to 30% available internationally — Canadian citizens/PRs only for international tenure)
Cannot have previously received a postdoctoral award from CIHR, NSERC, or SSHRC (including old Banting)
Maximum 3 applications allowed
Research program must be predominantly research-oriented and significantly different from doctoral thesis

benefits: Can be held at academic research institutions, research hospitals, colleges, NGOs, or Indigenous organizations in Canada or abroad (conditions apply)
Additional supplements may be available for priority areas, Black postdoctoral researchers, and Indigenous researchers
scholarships.target_group: Outstanding early-career researchers (within 3 years of PhD) from Canada and internationally who are pursuing postdoctoral research at Canadian institutions, across health, natural sciences, engineering, and social sciences.
scholarships.description: The Canada Postdoctoral Research Award (CPRA) is the successor to the discontinued Banting Postdoctoral Fellowship, providing CAD $70,000/year for 2 years to outstanding postdoctoral researchers. Administered jointly by CIHR, NSERC, and SSHRC, it supports researchers at Canadian and select international institutions. Up to 20% of awards are available to international applicants who are enrolled or conducting postdocs at Canadian institutions.
application_process: Select the funding agency matching your research field: CIHR (health), NSERC (natural sciences/engineering), SSHRC (social sciences/humanities)
Check institutional deadlines — your host institution may have an internal nomination deadline well before the agency deadline
Apply via the relevant agency online platform: CIHR (ResearchNET), NSERC (online system), SSHRC (Registration and login)
International applicants must apply through a Canadian institution — direct applications not accepted
Submission must be complete and on time — late applications are not accepted
Results announced: March 31
Contacts: CIHR: support-soutien@cihr-irsc.gc.ca | NSERC: nsercscholarships-boursescrsng@nserc-crsng.gc.ca | SSHRC: fellowships@sshrc-crsh.gc.ca
